The '''''Samarth''-class offshore patrol vessel''' are a series of eleven [[offshore patrol vessel]]s being built by [[Goa Shipyard Limited]] for the [[Indian Coast Guard]]. The construction of ''Samarth'' class was motivated by a desire to triple the Coast Guard assets in the aftermath of [[2008 Mumbai attacks]]. They are an improvement over the earlier {{sclass|Sankalp|offshore patrol vessel|4}}, with a larger beam and more powerful engines.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mazumdar|first1=Mrityunjoy|title=India's 20/20 vision: Coastguard joins the premier league|journal=IHS Jane's Navy International|date=1 May 2012|volume=117|issue=4|publisher=[[Jane's Information Group]]|location=Coulsdon|issn=2048-3457}}</ref><ref name="jfs-1617">{{cite book|editor1-last=Saunders|editor1-first=Stephen|editor1-mask=Commodore Stephen Saunders|title=Jane's Fighting Ships 2016–2017|date=2016|publisher=[[Jane's Information Group]]|location=Coulsdon|isbn=978-0710631855|page=364|edition=119th|chapter=India}}</ref> The ships are being constructed in two batches—a batch of six ordered in May 2012 that was completed in December 2017 and a follow-on batch of five ordered in August 2016.

==History==
Following the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the [[Government of India|Indian Government]] initiated a program to triple the Indian Coast Guard force, assets and infrastructure.<ref name="DefNow">{{cite web |url=http://www.defencenow.com/news/678/goa-shipyard-signs-contract-to-build-six-vessels-for-indian-coast-guard.html |title=Goa Shipyard Signs Contract to Build Six Vessels for Indian Coast Guard |website=Defence Now |year=2012 |access-date=19 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604195236/http://www.defencenow.com/news/678/goa-shipyard-signs-contract-to-build-six-vessels-for-indian-coast-guard.html |archive-date=4 June 2016}}</ref> Thereafter in accordance with it a 'request for information' for acquisition of six offshore patrol vessels was issued by the [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]] on 1 April 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://2.imimg.com/data2/QX/TC/HTT-240/240_2010-04-01_213181.pdf |title=Request for information |website=Indian Ministry of Defence |date=1 April 2010 |access-date=19 May 2014}}</ref> After technical evaluation and commercial bids a contract worth $400 million or Rs. 1800 crore was signed with GSL on 9 May 2012 to build six vessels.<ref name="DefNow"/>

In August 2016, a follow-on consisting of five patrol vessels was placed for INR 20 billion.<ref name="janes63503"/> The follow-on vessels will have a greater indigenous content of 70% compared to the 62% of the previous batch.<ref name="jni-22dec17">{{cite news|last1=Mazumdar|first1=Mrityunjoy|title=Indian Coast Guard commissions last of six Samarth-class OPVs|url=http://www.janes.com/article/76617/indian-coast-guard-commissions-last-of-six-samarth-class-opvs|work=Jane's Navy International|date=21 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222104823/http://www.janes.com/article/76617/indian-coast-guard-commissions-last-of-six-samarth-class-opvs|archive-date=22 December 2017}}</ref>

''Sachet'' the first OPV was launched on 21 February 2019<ref name="icgsachet"/> and commissioned on 15 May 2020 by Defence Minister [[Rajnath Singh]] by video conferencing.<ref name="Economic Times">{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/indian-coast-guard-patrol-vessel-2-interceptor-boats-commissioned/articleshow/75752488.cms|title=Indian Coast Guard patrol vessel, 2 interceptor boats commissioned|publisher=Economic Times|access-date=15 May 2020}}</ref>

''Sujeet'' the second OPV from the second batch was handed to [[Indian Coast Guard]] on 12 November 2020 and later commissioned on 15 December 2020.<ref name="suj_deliver">{{cite web|url=http://www.uniindia.com/gsl-makes-another-ahead-of-schedule-delivery-of-new-class-opv/west/news/2232925.html|title=GSL makes another ahead of schedule delivery of new class OPV|publisher=UNI India|date=12 November 2020}}</ref>

''Sajag'' the third OPV was delivered ahead of time on 16 March 2021. The ship was commissioned by [[National Security Advisor (India)|NSA]] [[Ajit Doval]] on May 29, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.psuconnect.in/news/gsl-makes-another-ahead-of-scheduled-delivery-of-new-class-opv/27002|title=GSL makes another ahead of scheduled delivery of new class OPV PSU NEWS|publisher=PSUConnect|date=16 March 2021}}</ref><ref name="sajag-comm">{{cite web|url=https://www.aninews.in/news/national/general-news/nsa-doval-to-commission-indian-coast-guards-ship-sajag-today20210529091157/|title=NSA Doval to commission Indian Coast Guard's ship Sajag today|publisher=ANI|date=2021-05-29}}</ref>

''Sarthak'' was delivered ahead of schedule and was commissioned in the [[Indian Coast Guard]] on 28 October 2021.<ref name="sarthak-comm"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/gsl-delivers-patrol-vessel-to-coast-guard-ahead-of-schedule/articleshow/86717709.cms|title=GSL delivers patrol vessel to Coast Guard ahead of schedule|publisher=Times Of India|date=2021-10-03}}</ref>

''Saksham'' the last ship of the project was delivered ahead of schedule on 8 February 2022. All 5 ships of the Fleet 2 were delivered ahead of schedule.<ref name="saksham_delivered">{{cite web|url=https://www.psuconnect.in/news/gsl-delivers-5th-and-last-vessel-of-5-cgopv-project/31231|title=GSL delivers 5th and last vessel of 5 CGOPV Project|publisher=PSU Connect|date=2022-02-08}}</ref>

==Description==
The class is {{convert|105|m|ftin}} long with a [[Displacement (ship)|displacement]] of 2,350 tonnes. Features include Integrated Bridge System, Integrated Machinery Control System, Power Management System and High Power External Fire Fighting System. They are designed to carry one twin engine Light Helicopter and five high speed boats including two [[Palfinger Marine|Palfinger]]<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://english.mathrubhumi.com/news/india/shoor-adds-teeth-to-coast-guard%25E2%2580%2599s-policing-patrolling-ops-english-news-1.987348 |title=Shoor adds teeth to Coast Guard's policing, patrolling ops |newspaper=[[Mathrubhumi]] |date=11 April 2016 |access-date=11 April 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415141721/http://english.mathrubhumi.com/news/india/shoor-adds-teeth-to-coast-guard%E2%80%99s-policing-patrolling-ops-english-news-1.987348 |archive-date=15 April 2016 }}</ref> QRIBs for fast boarding operations, search and rescue, law enforcement and maritime patrol. The class is also capable of carrying pollution response equipment to combat oil spill contamination at sea.<ref name="ToI51782844">{{Cite news |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Indian-Coast-Guard-offshore-patrol-vessel-Shoor-commissioned/articleshow/51782844.cms |title=Indian Coast Guard offshore patrol vessel Shoor commissioned |first=Narayan |last=Namboodiri |date=11 April 2016 |newspaper=The Times of India |access-date=11 April 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160412201754/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Indian-Coast-Guard-offshore-patrol-vessel-Shoor-commissioned/articleshow/51782844.cms |archive-date=12 April 2016 }}</ref>

== Service history ==
On 17 July 2024, the Indian Coast Guard carried out a rescue operation of the Indian fishing boat ''Aashni''. The boat, with 11 crew and around {{convert|80|nmi}} from [[Kochi]], [[Kerala]], faced heavy rain and challenging weather conditions. Due to loss of propulsion and flooding from a hull rupture close to the [[keel]], the vessel was in a serious situation. A [[Dornier 228]] surveillance aircraft of the ICG located the vessel on the night of 16 July 2024. ICGS ''Saksham'' was immediately diverted towards its location after receiving an order from the ICG District Headquarters No 4 (Kerala & Mahe). Eventually, ICGS ''Abhinav'', an {{sclass|Aadesh|patrol vessel|1}}, was also deployed along with a [[HAL Dhruv]] helicopter. The technical team from the ICG assisted in the de-flooding operations and rescued the crew members and recovered the distressed the vessel. After the culmination of the operation, the boat was handed over to the Fisheries Department.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-17 |title=ICG rescues stranded Indian Fishing Boat, with 11 people onboard, off Kerala Coast |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2033895 |access-date=2024-07-19 |website=Press Information Bureau}}</ref>

On 19 July 2024, Maritime Rescue Coordination Center (MRCC) [[Mumbai]] of ICG received distress call from container carrier {{MV|Maersk Frankfurt}} about {{cvt|50|nmi}} off Karwar about a major fire on board. Immediately, {{ship|ICGS|Sachet||2}}, ''Sujeet'' and {{ICGS|Samrat||2}} along with a Dornier 228 aircraft and a HAL Dhruv helicopter were deployed by Coast Guard District HQ No 11 (Goa) for aerial surveillance operations. [[Samudra-class pollution control vessel|ICGS ''Samudra Prahari'']] also provided support. As of 20 July, after 12 hours of effort, the fire in the front section of the ship was suppressed but the fire in the midship section was ablaze. The ICG was preparing for the provision of dry chemical powder (DCP) bags and balls to support firefighting operations.<ref>{{Cite news |title=12 hours on, Indian Coast Guard ships battle fire onboard Maersk Frankfurt vessel in Arabian Sea |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/12-hours-on-indian-coast-guard-ships-battle-fire-onboard-maersk-frankfurt-vessel-in-arabian-sea/articleshow/111885070.cms |access-date=2024-07-20 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-20 |title=ICG ships fight fire on cargo vessel for over 12 hours near Karwar |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/defence-icg-ships-fight-fire-on-cargo-vessel-for-over-12-hours-near-karwar-3559402/ |access-date=2024-07-20 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref> As of 21 July, after 24 hours of distress call, the ship was {{cvt|17|nmi}} off Karwar and the ICG was battling smoke and small fires on board the container ship. The ICG decided to use DCP to douse the fire. One crew member died in the incident. The cause of the fire was expected to be a short circuit after which the fire spread to the cargo classified as International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) that was on board, according to a report. The ship was en route from [[Mundra Port]], India to the [[Port of Colombo]], Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-07-21 |title=Container vessel Maersk Frankfurt still on fire: 1 crew member dead |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/container-vessel-maersk-frankfurt-still-on-fire-1-crew-member-dead/articleshow/111892009.cms |access-date=2024-07-21 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> On 22 July, ICG's Deputy Inspector General  Bhatia confirmed that the fire was under control after using {{cvt|150|kg}} of DCP bags deployed from helicopters. There were no fire in the dangerous goods section of the ship. Small fires were still burning, but four vessels of ICG were near the ship and helicopters were taking routine visits. The ship was out of danger. No oil pollution was reported but adequate preparation was taken and the ICG asked Karnataka, Goa and Kerala to activate the pollution response mechanism.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fire On Merchant Navy Ship Off Goa Coast Under Control, Crew Member Dead |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/fire-on-merchant-navy-ship-off-goa-coast-under-control-crew-member-dead-6153307 |access-date=2024-07-22 |website=NDTV.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Day 3: Fire continues aboard container Maersk Frankfurt |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/goa/day-3-fire-continues-aboard-container-maersk-frankfurt/articleshow/111908837.cms |access-date=2024-07-22 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> By 30 July, Operation Sahayata was complete and a total of five ships, one Dornier aircraft and two Dhruv helicopters were deployed for the job. More than {{cvt|1200|kg}} of DCP was used. [[Thermography|Infrared images]] confirmed that hotspots has reduced and smoldering was reduced to one small part of the ship. There were no more pollution risks and the ship was stable and operational.<ref>{{Cite news  |date=2024-07-28 |title=MV Maersk Frankfurt that caught fire structurally stable after 10 days of fire fighting efforts |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/mv-maersk-frankfurt-that-caught-fire-structurally-stable-after-10-days-of-fire-fighting-efforts/article68457659.ece |access-date=2024-07-30 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

On 21 August 2024, ICGS ''Sujay'' made a port call with an integral helicopter in [[Jakarta]], Indonesia for a two-day visit.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-21 |title=ICGS Sujay makes port call in Indonesia for a two-day visit as part of overseas deployment to East Asia |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2047352 |access-date=2024-08-23 |website=Press Information Bureau}}</ref> On 4 September 2024, ''Sujay'' made another port call at [[Incheon]], South Korea. The ICG officials conducted professional interactions with the [[Korea Coast Guard]] (KCG) for topics like [[marine pollution]] response, maritime search and rescue and [[maritime law enforcement]]. The visit was a part of Indian Coast Guard's East Asia deployment and a [[memorandum of understanding]] (MoU) was signed between the ICG and KCG in 2006 for enhanced maritime cooperation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-04 |title=ICGS Sujay makes port call in South Korea as part of its ongoing overseas deployment to East Asia |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2051711 |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=Press Information Bureau}}</ref> On 18 September 204, ''Sujay'' reached [[Bali]], Indonesia, for a three-day visit. Formal discussions with the [[Indonesian Maritime Security Agency]] (IMSA) during the visit focused on operational turn around, marine pollution response, maritime search and rescue and maritime law enforcement. The visit was a result of an MoU signed between the ICG and BAKAMLA (IMSA) on 6 July 2020 to enhance maritime cooperation and institutionalised its cooperative engagements. The crew in this deployment included 10 [[National Cadet Corps (India)|National Cadet Corps]] (NCC).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-19 |title=Coast Guard ship Sujay reaches Bali, to take part in various maritime activities |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/indian-coast-guard-ship-sujay-reaches-bali-indonesia-host-of-maritime-activities-2602424-2024-09-19 |access-date=2024-09-19 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

On 9 December 2025, ICGS ''Sarthak'' reached [[Shuwaikh Port]], [[Kuwait]] for a four-day visit as part of her Overseas Deployment to the [[Persian Gulf|Gulf]] region.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=ICG Ship Sarthak Reaches Suwaikh Port in Kuwait |date=2025-12-09 |publisher=[[Press Information Bureau]] |url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2201078&reg=3&lang=1 |access-date=2025-12-12}}</ref>

ICGS ''Sarathi'' forms a part of the [[1st Training Squadron]] (1TS) of the [[Indian Navy]] and was part of the [[1st Training Squadron#2025|2025]] and [[1st Training Squadron#2026|2026]] Long Range Training Deployment (LRTD) flotilla to the South West Indian Ocean Region and [[South East Asia]]. The ship also took part in the [[International Fleet Review 2026]] held near [[Visakhapatnam]] on 18 February 2026.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=IFR & MILAN 2026 |url=https://www.ifrmilan26.com/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260219124733/https://www.ifrmilan26.com/ |archive-date=2026-02-19 |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=IFR & MILAN 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

extract: The Samarth-class offshore patrol vessel are a series of eleven offshore patrol vessels being built by Goa Shipyard Limited for the Indian Coast Guard. The construction of Samarth class was motivated by a desire to triple the Coast Guard assets in the aftermath of 2008 Mumbai attacks. They are an improvement over the earlier Sankalp class, with a larger beam and more powerful engines. The ships are being constructed in two batches—a batch of six ordered in May 2012 that was completed in December 2017 and a follow-on batch of five ordered in August 2016.
